facts.text: Euharlee’s name comes from Cherokee, meaning “she laughs as she runs,” a nod to the rhythmic flow of Euharlee Creek.
The town boasts Georgia’s oldest remaining covered bridge, listed on the National Register and part of the Georgia Covered Bridge Trail.
Just south of Euharlee, the towering cooling towers of Georgia Power’s Plant Bowen mark the state’s second‑largest coal‑fired power plant.
At the heart of downtown sits the Euharlee Welcome Center & History Museum, where visitors explore Cherokee roots to modern life through photos, videos, and quizzes.
Euharlee was officially incorporated on September 16, 1870, after settlers first called the area Burge’s Mill in the 1840s.
